D012-D016_h001.question:
I’ve been having this thing with spiders for about a year now, maybe a bit more. It’s not just that I don’t like them. What really gets to me are these thoughts that pop in my head, like if I even see a spider or step near where one might be, somehow it’ll crawl on me, lay eggs under my skin, or I’ll bring it home in the mail bag and it’ll hurt my wife or grandkids. I know it sounds irrational, but once it starts, I can’t switch it off.

On my route, if I see a web on a fence or letterbox, my heart jumps straight into my throat. I break out in a sweat, feel shaky, and sometimes I have to just stop and steady myself. Then I start doing these little rituals—checking my shoes over and over, shaking out the mailbag multiple times, avoiding certain houses, even going back to re-check the van to “make sure” there’s no spider inside. If I try not to do these checks, the anxiety just keeps building until I give in and do them.
D012-D016_h001.options:
A. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    B. Specific Phobia
    C. Bipolar II Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia

D012-D016_h002.question:
Most of what’s bothering me started a couple of years ago, but it’s gotten much worse over the last 8 or 9 months. I work in a gallery with huge glass windows, so I’m constantly thinking about storms. It’s not just that I’m scared of bad weather; my mind keeps jumping to these images of lightning hitting the building, the glass shattering, water pouring in, and people dying because I didn’t “prepare” properly. Once those thoughts start, I can’t shake them.

When I see dark clouds or even check the weather app, I feel this jolt of panic. I’ll stop what I’m doing and almost freeze up in the middle of the gallery. Sometimes I literally stand there, unable to move for a few minutes, running through all the terrible scenarios in my head. Then I start doing these little rituals to calm myself down—rechecking all the windows, unplugging electronics, counting to certain numbers, repeating phrases under my breath like, “It’ll be fine, it’ll be fine,” until it feels “right.”  

I know it doesn’t make logical sense, but I’m terrified that if I don’t do these things, the storm will be worse or something awful will happen.
D012-D016_h002.options:
A. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    B. Specific Phobia
    C. Bipolar II Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia

D012-D016_h003.question:
It started maybe a year ago, and it’s been getting worse over the past several months. I keep getting these images in my head of insects—especially spiders—crawling on me or getting into my ears or my kids’ mouths while they sleep. It’s not just “I don’t like spiders”; it turns into this whole chain of thoughts that they’re carrying some horrible disease, that I’ll bring them home on my clothes from work, and my family will get sick because I was careless.

Once that idea pops up, I can’t shut it off. Just thinking about maybe seeing a spider later in the day sets off this intense anxiety—my chest gets tight, my heart races. I’ll replay scenes of checking under desks or in corners at the tower, over and over in my mind, like I missed one.

To calm down, I find myself doing these ritual-like checks: scanning every corner of a room, shaking out my clothes multiple times before I leave work, rechecking the kids’ beds and windows at night. I know it’s excessive and irrational, but if I don’t do it, the anxiety gets almost unbearable.
D012-D016_h003.options:
A. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    B. Specific Phobia
    C. Bipolar II Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia

D012-D016_h004.question:
It’s mainly storms for me. Thunder, lightning, heavy rain. But it’s not just that I’m scared of storms themselves—it’s what I can’t get out of my head about them. For about the last two years, I’ve had these images of our house getting struck, burning down, my kids trapped inside. Once those thoughts start, I can’t shut them off. Even on a clear day, if I see clouds on the forecast, I start getting worked up, shaky, heart racing, like the danger is already here.

At work on the factory floor, I’ll sneak looks at the weather app over and over, sometimes every few minutes, just to “make sure.” At home, if there’s any mention of rain, I unplug things, check the fuse box, go around the house closing windows, rechecking the smoke alarms—sometimes three, four times in a row because it doesn’t feel “right” yet.

I know it sounds over the top, but if I don’t do these routines, I feel like I’m personally inviting something terrible to happen to my family.
D012-D016_h004.options:
A. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    B. Specific Phobia
    C. Bipolar II Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia

D012-D016_h005.question:
It started maybe three, four years ago, but it’s gotten much worse over the last year. I work nights as a security guard in a big warehouse, so I’m alone a lot, and that’s when it really hits me.

I can’t stop getting these thoughts that something terrible will happen if there’s a storm or if it gets too dark. Not just normal worry—my mind starts playing these pictures of the roof collapsing in a storm, or flood water rushing in and drowning my coworkers or my grandkids at home. It feels like if I don’t do certain things, it’ll be my fault.

So I keep checking the weather app over and over—sometimes every few minutes. I walk the perimeter again and again to make sure doors and windows are shut “just right.” At home, if I hear thunder on the forecast, I unplug everything, triple-check the basement for water, and make my wife sleep with a flashlight nearby. If I try to stop, my heart races, I get short of breath, sweaty, shaky—almost like a panic attack—until I give in and do the checking and re-checking.
D012-D016_h005.options:
A. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    B. Specific Phobia
    C. Bipolar II Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia

D012-D016_h006.question:
It really started about a year ago. I get these thoughts, out of nowhere, that if I drive over a bridge, the car will suddenly go off the side and my kids will die and it will be my fault. It’s not just, “bridges are scary”; it’s like this whole movie in my head that I can’t shut off. I try to tell myself it’s irrational, but the thought just keeps looping.

When I know I have to cross a bridge or go through a long tunnel, I’ll start panicking before I even get there—heart racing, hands sweating, sometimes I feel like I can’t breathe. I still force myself to do it because I have to take the kids to school and appointments, but the whole time I’m gripping the wheel, checking the mirrors over and over, driving in the exact center of the lane, counting to ten repeatedly, and saying little phrases under my breath, like, “Stay safe, stay safe,” until it’s over. I feel like if I don’t do those things, something terrible will happen.  

It’s exhausting and embarrassing, and it’s starting to affect how and where I’m willing to drive.
D012-D016_h006.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Specific Phobia
    C. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D012-D016_h007.question:
It started about a year ago, after I interpreted a really graphic medical appointment. Ever since then, I can’t get these images out of my head—blood, needles snapping, veins bursting. It’s like a loop I can’t shut off. I’ll be washing dishes and suddenly I’m imagining cutting myself and bleeding out, even though I don’t want that at all. Then I feel like if I don’t do certain things, it might actually happen.

Now, any time I know I have to get bloodwork or even bring my kids to the pediatrician, I freeze. I literally can’t move for a moment; my legs feel like concrete. My heart races, I feel dizzy, sometimes I think I’ll faint. I still go, because I have to, but the whole time I’m silently counting, praying in a specific order, and clenching and unclenching my fingers in patterns to “keep everyone safe.” If I don’t do that, I’m terrified something horrible will happen and it will be my fault, even though I know how irrational that sounds.
D012-D016_h007.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Specific Phobia
    C. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D012-D016_h008.question:
I’ve been a postman over 25 years, so I’m used to dogs, bad weather, all that. What’s gotten out of hand is this thing with blood and needles, but it’s not just being squeamish. 

For about a year now, I keep getting these thoughts that if I see blood—mine or anyone’s—or if someone sticks a needle in me, I’ll somehow get infected and then bring something home to my wife and kids. It plays in my head like a movie I can’t shut off: me brushing against a railing with dried blood on it, then touching the mail, then our door handle, and everyone getting sick.  

Because of that, I’ve started doing all these little “rituals.” I wash my hands over and over after touching letterboxes that look dirty, I check my skin repeatedly to make sure there’s no cut or spot of blood, and I avoid walking past the medical clinic on my route. If I even think about the flu shot or blood tests, my heart races and I’ll reroute my deliveries so I don’t see the clinic. I’ve turned down checkups and even skipped family gatherings at hospitals, which is starting to cause problems at work and at home.
D012-D016_h008.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Specific Phobia
    C. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D012-D016_h009.question:

So before I go on a bridge I find myself checking the weather over and over, rereading traffic reports, sometimes repeating phrases under my breath or tapping the steering wheel a certain number of times “to keep it safe.”

I still force myself to go when I have a meeting or a deadline, but I’m shaking the whole time, breathing fast, clutching the wheel, trying to “neutralize” the thoughts with these little rituals. It’s exhausting and takes up way too much of my day.

D012-D016_h010.question:

I can’t really leave the situation, so I end up just freezing and powering through it, but I’m completely on edge until it’s gone.

What really bothers me is what’s going on in my head around it. Then I feel compelled to act on that: I’ll go wash my hands over and over, check my scrubs, re-sterilize things I already cleaned, or mentally replay the scene. I know it’s irrational, but the thoughts and the rituals feel impossible to resist.

D012-D016_h011.question:

I keep getting these images in my head of accidentally cutting a client so deep they bleed a lot, or somehow giving them an infection that kills them. I wipe my tools over and over, way more than we’re required to, and wash my hands repeatedly before each client until they’re dry and cracked. If I nick someone even a tiny bit, I replay it in my head all night, checking pictures of my station, Googling infections, sometimes even messaging the client to “make sure they’re okay.”

I’ve begun avoiding clients who want anything involving cuticle cutting or sharp tips. I’ll make excuses or switch them to someone else because I’m afraid if I don’t do all my checking and cleaning just right, something terrible will happen.

D012-D016_h012.question:

D012-D016_h014.question:

D012-D016_h015.question:

D012-D016_h016.question:

It’s these thoughts that get stuck in my head that if I get in an elevator, I’ll somehow lose control and hurt someone, or the elevator will trap me and I’ll go crazy and start attacking people. I know it sounds irrational, but the thoughts feel so real and intense I can’t shut them off.

Before I even go near an elevator at school or the subway, I have to do these little routines in my head—counting to certain numbers, repeating certain phrases silently—until it “feels right,” or I’m convinced nothing bad will happen. If I don’t, I’m sure something awful will. When I can’t avoid elevators, I’ll only go in if a friend comes with me and stands on my right side, holding my backpack; that’s become kind of a “safe” setup. I’m not just scared of the elevator—I’m scared of what my own thoughts might make happen if I don’t do these rituals.
